rounds.fact: TechCrunch launched in 2005 covering Silicon Valley startups specifically, and became so influential that a positive TechCrunch writeup could meaningfully affect a young company's funding prospects.
Barnes & Noble launched bn.com in 1997 specifically to compete with Amazon, one of the first major traditional retailers to take online bookselling seriously.
EarthLink grew into one of the largest ISPs of the dial-up era by positioning itself as friendlier and more customer-focused than AOL, its biggest rival.
Plenty of Fish was famously built and run by a single person for years, supported entirely by ads, before eventually being sold for hundreds of millions of dollars.
ABC News's early website tried to translate its broadcast anchors' star power onto the web, with a design that prioritized video clips even when most users were still on dial-up.
